title: Inpatient Rounds Language Access: A Workflow Guide for LEP Patients
summary: Learn how to run inpatient rounds with patients who have limited English proficiency, from pre-round setup and interpreted bedside discussion to.
body_markdown:
###


Start interpretation before the bedside presentation when the patient and team do not share enough language for the conversation. Keep it active for the clinically relevant discussion, patient questions, and changes to the plan.


###


Long turns increase the amount of information the interpreter has to hold before speaking. Research on family-centered rounds has linked longer pre-interpretation segments with greater information loss.


###


For information that affects the patient's care plan, interpreting only the final summary can remove the patient's chance to correct information or participate while the decision is being made.


###


Yes. AI medical interpretation can support real-time bedside communication during rounds and follow-up conversations when the system is built for clinical use and has appropriate quality controls.


###


Track whether interpretation is active before the presentation, time to active interpretation, patient questions, repeated clarification after rounds, communication-related safety events, and patient understanding of the daily plan.
